turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

The boxes are mostly corrugated cardboard, which is actually really bad for the environment if you don't recycle it right. I took this environmental science class for a semester at community college before I started this job, and the professor—Mr. Davis, he always wore these awful brown corduroy jackets—he said cardboard takes up way too much space in landfills. Did you know that? They use a lot of tape on our boxes too, the heavy-duty clear kind that just ruins your work gloves if you aren't careful.

If you don't wear gloves, they just slide right out of your hands. I lost my favorite pair of work gloves last week. They were leather, really nice ones my dad gave me. He bought them at a hardware store that went out of business a few years ago. It's a shame, too, because that hardware store had the best selection of screws and nails. You could buy them loose out of these little wooden bins instead of having to buy a whole plastic clamshell package just to get two screws. I hate those clamshell packages. You need a pair of scissors just to open the scissors you bought, it makes no sense. I sliced my thumb open trying to open a package of AA batteries once. Batteries are so expensive now. I remember when you could get a whole pack of them at the dollar store, but now they're like five bucks just for four of them. And they don't even last as long. I put some in my TV remote and they were dead in a month...

The lawnmower we had was this old gas-powered thing that you had to pull the cord like ten times before it would finally start, and it always smelled like gasoline and cut grass. But now they have those little rubber things on the nozzles that trap the fumes, which I guess is better for the environment. The environment is really important, you know? Like all those plastic rings from soda packs that get stuck on turtles' necks in the ocean. I always make sure to cut mine up with scissors before I throw them away. I have this pair of heavy-duty kitchen shears I use for everything. They can cut right through chicken bones, which is great when I'm making stock. Making your own chicken stock is way better than buying those boxes at the store. The store-bought stuff always has way too much sodium. You have to watch your sodium intake, otherwise your blood pressure goes up. My uncle had high blood pressure and he had to start eating this special salt substitute that tasted like chemicals...
